articles.title: Research
articles.content:
November 20, 2026

Introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that tests how well AI models read molecular structures, interpret experimental results, and choose which compounds to test next.

00:00

We’re introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that evaluates AI models on reasoning tasks drawn from medicinal chemistry research. It tests whether models can connect a molecule’s structure with experimental evidence to explain results, compare compounds, and predict their properties. Building AI that can reliably support this work is one step towards helping scientists develop better medicines.

One of the hardest parts of this work is that improving one property of a molecule can make another worse. A compound might act strongly against a disease related protein but be poorly absorbed or break down too quickly in the body. Medicinal chemists work through these tradeoffs by designing, making, and testing related compounds, then deciding what to try next. For AI to help, it needs to connect changes in molecular structure with experimental evidence and reason about what compounds are worth pursuing.

MedChemBench measures these abilities through 99 problems drawn from published research. At the xhigh reasoning setting, GPT‑6.2 Astra earned 84.5% of the available credit, compared with 83.3% for GPT‑6 Astra, 82.0% for GPT‑6.1 Sol, and 58.2% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. GPT‑6 Astra was strongest at reconstructing molecular structures and explaining experimental evidence. Selecting compounds and predicting their numerical properties proved harder for that model.

MedChemBench draws on 117 papers and patents and includes 761 distinct molecular structures. For most problems, models receive the context available at a chosen point in a research program: the biological target, the researchers’ goals, the compounds studied so far, and selected experimental findings.

The benchmark evaluates four components:

Molecular structures.Correct atom connections and specified stereochemistry in molecules assembled from the drawings and chemical groups provided.

Scientific reasoning.Explanations supported by the supplied evidence, such as the reasons for choosing one compound over another.

Ranking and selection.Compound rankings and choices that meet the stated requirements.

Property predictions.Agreement with the numerical values and categories reported in the source material, including measured and calculated molecular properties.

One MedChemBench problem draws on research into inhibitors of PRMT5, a protein studied in cancer drug discovery. The model receives molecular structures and results from earlier experiments. It must predict how three related compounds will behave: how strongly they block PRMT5 in cells, how readily they cross a cell barrier, and how quickly liver enzymes break them down in a laboratory assay.Later experiments, withheld from the model, showed a tradeoff. Compound 23 blocked PRMT5 in cells at a lower concentration, while compound 24 crossed the cell barrier more readily and broke down more slowly in the liver-enzyme assay.

Predicting these properties together tests whether a model can connect molecular structures with several aspects of compound behavior. This reflects a central challenge in medicinal chemistry: stronger activity against a target does not necessarily come with better permeability or slower breakdown.The benchmark checks whether the model reconstructs the molecular structures correctly and how closely its predictions match experimental measurements. Predictions receive partial credit based on their closeness to the measured values. Measurements already supplied in the prompt must also be reproduced correctly.

00:00

Small chemical changes can produce different property profiles. The task asks models to connect the structures with evidence about their behavior.

Before a model can reason about a compound’s properties, it needs to identify the molecule correctly. Chemical drawings encode atom connections, ring structures, and stereochemistry.

MedChemBench tests whether models preserve this information when reconstructing molecules from the drawings and chemical groups provided.

One problem asks models to assemble a molecule from a central structure and two attached groups while preserving an 18-atom ring. At the highest reasoning setting shared by all eleven models (xhigh), GPT‑6 Astra reconstructed this compound correctly in all ten responses. GPT‑5.6 Sol and GPT‑5.6 Luna failed across all ten responses.

In the illustrated answers, GPT‑5.6 Sol produced a 15-atom ring, while GPT‑5.6 Luna split the molecule into two disconnected fragments.

These errors change the identity of the molecule being analyzed. This example tests a foundation of medicinal chemistry reasoning: whether the model can accurately represent the compound before interpreting its behavior.

Figure 1. The same input, different molecules

These selected answers for compound 17 show a correct reconstruction, a smaller ring, and disconnected fragments.

While measuring the benchmark for structure components, Astra earned 95.4% of the available credit at xhigh. This result shows strong performance on reconstructing the molecular structures supplied in the tasks.

We evaluated eleven GPT models at different reasoning-effort settings. Across the full benchmark, Astra earned 83.3% of the available credit at the shared xhigh setting, compared with 82.0% for GPT‑6.1 Sol, 75.1% for GPT‑6.1 Terra, and 58.2% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. At max effort, GPT‑6 Astra reached 83.8%. Higher reasoning settings improved scores, while large differences between models remained. The figure below plots performance against output tokens.

Figure 2. Performance versus token usage

Each point represents a model at one reasoning setting, showing 51 combinations across nine models from GPT‑5.6 onward. Scores are averaged across 99 problems; bars show 95% uncertainty intervals. Tokens include reasoning and the final answer.

The component results separate four abilities: reconstructing molecules, explaining findings, selecting compounds, and predicting measurements. This shows where models are strongest and where errors remain.

Figure 3. Component performance versus token usage

Astra’s clearest strengths were in reconstructing molecular structures and explaining the scientific evidence. In selected reasoning examples from our preprint, Astra correctly identified structural changes and weighed their possible effects on protein binding, absorption, and metabolism.

Where selection and prediction remain difficult, Astra earned 95.4% of the available structure credit at xhigh, but only about half the credit for selecting compounds and predicting numerical properties. These categories use different tasks and scoring rules, but the results show substantial room to improve predictions and compound choices.

These results do not establish whether models can discover new drugs or improve laboratory decisions. Prior exposure to the published sources cannot be ruled out, and each response was a single attempt without tools, feedback, or new experiments. While the benchmark evaluates reasoning from historical evidence rather than real-world drug discovery, its results help identify where models are advancing and where challenges remain. We believe MedChemBench will support continued progress and look forward to sharing updates as our models advance to serve the field.

GPT‑6 Astra는 구조 복원과 실험 결과 설명에 강했지만, 화합물 선택과 수치적 물성 예측은 상대적으로 어려웠다. 신약 탐색에서 여러 물성의 상충관계를 다루는 능력을 점검한다는 의미가 있으며, 이 점수가 실제 의약품 개발 성과를 입증하는 것은 아니다.

articles.title: NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a Continuous Diffusion Language Model with 14 checkpoints at 3B/8B
articles.content: NVIDIA has released Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a collection of 14 open checkpoints at 3B and 8B scale. Nemotron-Labs-Sigma is a continuous diffusion language model family that denoises text in a 16-D embedding space. Most diffusion LLMs, such as LLaDA and Dream, work on discrete tokens. Sigma works in a smooth latent space instead. NVIDIA team states that this makes few-step distillation and trajectory steering practical for text. TL;DR Size: 3B and 8B parameters, 14 checkpoints. Context is 4,096 tokens (8,192 for Sigma-8B-instruct). Runs on: 1 NVIDIA GPU in bfloat16 (Ampere, Lovelace, Hopper, Blackwell). About 120 to 140 tokens/s on 1 H100. No CPU support, no quantized variants listed. Performance: Sigma-8B base averages 71.16 on NVIDIA’s 6-task suite, ahead of NLD-8B (70.22). Best: 91.96 on GSM8K (Sigma-8B-instruct, 256 DDPM steps). Worst: 17.00 on AIME25 (same model and sampler). Bottom line: Best: the 8-step distilled 8B keeps a 70.34 average. Worst: the instruct average (59.14) trails NLD-8B (59.92). What is Nemotron-Labs-Sigma? The research team calls Sigma the first large-scale family of continuous diffusion language models. The collection has 4 variant types at each size: Base: Sigma-3B and Sigma-8B. Instruct: Sigma-3B-instruct and Sigma-8B-instruct. Few-step distilled: distill-3B and distill-8B at NFE 2, 4, 8 and 16 (8 checkpoints). Self-speculative: distill-spec-3B and distill-spec-8B. How does continuous diffusion for language work? Each token maps to a point in a learned 16-D embedding space. Training adds Gaussian noise to these embeddings and teaches the model to remove it. The embedding geometry is learned jointly with the denoiser. Generation runs blockwise. Each denoised block is committed to a KV cache before the next starts. Blocks default to 64 tokens. The backbone is a Ministral-style decoder-only Transformer with grouped-query attention, SwiGLU and rotary embeddings. Training starts from an autoregressive warm start of about 1T tokens. About 0.3T tokens of diffusion training follow. At inference, classifier-free guidance and score temperature matter most. The model card page recommends guidance 3 and temperature 0.3 at 32 DDIM steps. Why does a continuous space matter? Discrete diffusion jumps between token states, so its trajectories are hard to steer. Sigma follows smooth ODE/SDE paths instead. Per the research paper, these degrade gracefully at low step counts and distill efficiently. Embedding-space steering also tunes the quality-diversity trade-off for pass@k sampling. How does Sigma perform on benchmarks? On the research’s 6-task base suite, Sigma-8B with 256 DDPM steps averages 71.16. NLD-8B in diffusion mode scores 70.22, Dream-7B 58.74 and LLaDA-8B 41.78. Qwen3-8B in AR mode scores 68.91. A cheaper 32-step DDIM sampler still gives Sigma-8B a 70.18 average. Coding is the standout. Sigma-8B scores 65.12 on HumanEval versus 62.80 for NLD-8B. MBPP is weaker, at 65.74 versus 67.00. After SFT, Sigma-8B-instruct scores 91.96 on GSM8K, 78.40 on MATH-500 and 82.50 on HumanEval. Hard reasoning stays limited, at 23.33 on AIME24 and 17.00 on AIME25. Its 10-task average of 59.14 sits just below NLD-8B at 59.92. All scores are NVIDIA’s own evaluations. articles.title: RadixArk Ships DaisyRose-27B, a 27B Agentic Coding Model Trained With Reinforcement Learning Only
articles.content: This week RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B, its first open-weight model. DaisyRose-27B is an agentic coding model from RadixArk, post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B with reinforcement learning (RL). The model card page states that it used RL only, with no SFT or distillation. It ships under Apache 2.0 as a drop-in replacement for the base model. The main result: Terminal Bench 4.1 pass@1 rises from 5.6 to 12.0. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension. TL;DR Size: 27.8B dense parameters (0.46B vision encoder, 0.42B MTP head), 262,144-token context. Runs on: 1 GPU. BF16 is about 52 GB, FP8 about 29 GB, NVFP4 about 23 GB (Blackwell only). Listed targets: H200, B200, GB300, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, DGX Spark. GGUF also available. Performance: Beats its Qwen3.8-27B base on all 7 reported benchmarks. Best: IFBench 82.4, the top score among the 9 models RadixArk compared. Worst: HLE (text only) 34.3, only +0.4 over the base and below Inkling 2 Small’s 44.1. Bottom line: Best: Terminal Bench 4.1 more than doubles after 18 days of RL. Worst: it still trails much larger MoE models on hard agentic tasks. What is DaisyRose-27B? DaisyRose-27B keeps the Qwen3.8-27B architecture unchanged. The model card lists 64 decoder layers in a 3:1 pattern. Three Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers alternate with 1 full-attention layer. Hidden size is 5,120. A 27-layer vision encoder handles images. One multi-token-prediction layer supports speculative decoding. Input is text and images, output is text, and it is a thinking model. How was DaisyRose-27B trained? RadixArk built about 1,200 curated tasks with Eigent AI, chosen from thousands of candidates. Each task targets a specific failure of the base model. Each sandbox attempt allows up to 1.5 hours, 100+ tool calls and 256k+ output tokens. Agent sessions reach up to 1M tokens, per the blog. Training ran on Miles, RadixArk’s open-source RL framework, in fully asynchronous mode. The run used 144 H200 GPUs for 18 days. Of those, 128 handled agent inference and 16 handled training. Total compute was 63,000 GPU-hours. RadixArk reports 37% MFU on its internal backend. An open-source Megatron-based trainer reached 16%. End-to-end throughput was 16.8k tokens/s versus 8.3k, a 2.0x speedup. RadixArk says this cut GPU time by 57%. Sandboxes ran on AgentENV. RadixArk reports about 944,000 sandboxes from mid-September to mid-November. Peak concurrency hit 1,566. Creation success was 99% over 9 weeks. RadixArk puts the cost about 80% below popular cloud sandbox providers. How does DaisyRose-27B perform on benchmarks? All scores are self-reported by RadixArk. DaisyRose scores are the higher of its BF16 and FP8 runs. articles.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25011v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way.
  The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.
articles.summary: 학습이론의 오래된 표본 압축 문제에 대해, VC 차원이 d인 모든 이진 개념 클래스에 크기 O(d² log² d)의 압축 체계를 구성할 수 있다는 연구가 나왔다. 연구진은 기존의 d에 대한 지수적 상한을 다항식 상한으로 개선해, 표본 압축 추측의 약한 형태를 증명했다고 보고했다. 이는 적은 학습 표본으로 예측기를 표현하는 능력과 일반화 사이의 관계를 이해하는 데 중요한 이론적 진전이다. 다만 O(d) 크기를 요구하는 원래의 더 강한 추측을 해결한 것은 아니며, 제시된 자료는 arXiv 초록이다.

articles.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24963v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Do standard benchmarks see the architectural differences that matter? We study it with 64 from-scratch pretraining runs of Transformers and three linear-model families at 1.3-8B parameters on 1-2T Nemotron-CC tokens, at a cost of roughly 100k USD per 8B run.
  In academic-scale pretraining (1.3B parameters, 100B tokens), architectural differences can all but disappear when the models are carefully tuned. Instead, at 1-2T tokens they become measurable: Canon layers, which add local token mixing, consistently improve Transformers, saving about 30% of pretraining tokens for the same MMLU accuracy at 8B. We also introduce GLA5 and GDN2, which improve gated linear attention and Gated DeltaNet with low-rank output gates. Surprisingly, with Canon, the simplest linear model, gated linear attention, matches Gated DeltaNet and outperforms Mamba2 even at 8B/1T. Therefore, the extra machinery of Gated DeltaNet and Mamba2 may do little more than mix neighboring tokens.
  Even at 8B/1T, however, high scores on standard benchmarks can hide weaknesses in basic in-context skills. In particular, linear models that match or beat Transformers on these benchmarks cannot, in fact, reliably retrieve information from a short 500-token context. Moreover, no model, Transformer or linear, reliably beats random guessing on arguably the simplest two-hop question, stated in a few short sentences, even at this scale.
  These findings $\textbf{challenge traditional architecture research}$ based primarily on standard benchmark scores. In contrast, small synthetic playgrounds, which predicted the architectural differences above at <100M parameters, can reveal what these benchmarks miss. For practitioners, one lesson is to include in-context reasoning examples in pretraining data from an early stage, rather than reserve them for later mid-training, let alone post-training.
articles.summary: 13억~80억 매개변수 모델을 대상으로 64회의 사전학습 실험을 수행한 연구가, 국소 토큰 혼합을 추가하는 Canon 계층의 효과와 표준 벤치마크의 한계를 분석했다. 80억 매개변수 Transformer에서는 같은 MMLU 정확도에 도달하는 데 필요한 사전학습 토큰을 약 30% 줄였다고 보고했다. 반면 표준 평가에서 Transformer와 대등하거나 앞선 선형 모델도 500토큰 문맥의 정보 검색을 안정적으로 수행하지 못했고, 실험한 모델들은 단순한 두 단계 추론에서도 취약성을 보였다. 아키텍처 선택 시 종합 점수뿐 아니라 문맥 내 검색·추론 능력을 별도로 검증해야 한다는 시사점을 준다.

articles.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
articles.content: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared—and widely misinterpreted, owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. One of the biggest questions in AI right now is the extent to which progress on “verifiable” tasks—where it’s possible to check automatically whether an AI system has succeeded or failed—carry over into tasks on which success or failure is harder to measure. We know how to teach neural networks how to do verifiable tasks: Researchers have the systems attempt one many times, strengthen the neural pathways that contribute to success, and weaken the pathways that contribute to failures. That’s why AI systems have become so good at coding and math, two domains where it’s possible to determine automatically whether a solution does or doesn’t work. It’s much harder to apply this technique, known as reinforcement learning, to tasks where success is less well defined or takes longer to ascertain—such as choosing a new research direction. For the same reason, it’s tough to evaluate AI performance on these tasks, so METR’s original time horizon plot didn’t include any of them. But it’s precisely this type of task that will prove essential if AI systems are to automate research and development. And AI research and development is an especially hot topic right now. Parts of the AI community are still reeling from a different, heavily redacted METR report from earlier this month, which claimed that AI might be speeding up the pace of AI progress at Anthropic by a factor of two. That report sparked fears that the company (which just had a blockbuster IPO) could soon achieve full recursive self-improvement, a regime in which AI systems autonomously design their own successors with no human involvement. METR researchers have worked to make sure their new suite of tasks includes some of the fuzzier, judgment-laden ones that could be most relevant to AI research and development. In one task, they ask models to design new AI evaluations that METR could use in its research and then have human METR employees score the results. Even though the most advanced models are now better than almost every human at software engineering, here they fall short: Not one of the AI-designed evaluations was good enough for METR employees to consider it useful for their research. In another task, models have to score philosophical arguments. This task is intended to capture the extent to which models can exercise good judgment—though METR writes in the report that employees disagree about how relevant the task is for automation of AI R&D. On this task, too, models fell short of human performance. Though it’s difficult to score these new tasks—and even harder to determine what the scores mean—experts I spoke with appreciate that METR is incorporating new types of evaluations into its work. “We’re at the point where AI evaluations need to get more creative,” says Sayash Kapoor, a computer scientist and incoming professor at UC Berkeley. “Trying to push the envelope of the space of evaluations is a welcome change.” Kapoor says he wasn’t surprised to see that models fall short of performance on more open-ended tasks, such as designing an AI evaluation—in a preprint from August, he and his collaborators reported that AI models are not yet able to reproduce human computer science research on their own. And in a Wednesday blog post, OpenAI reported that its models don’t do as well on the real-world tasks its employees assign them as they do on the easier, more verifiable tasks in METR’s original suite. Still, people disagree about how to interpret current performance differences on easily verifiable and hard-to-verify tasks, Kapoor says. Though he thinks that research taste—the ability to choose promising questions, hypotheses, and experiments—will prove a major bottleneck in automating AI R&D, others contend that models trained on easy-to-verify tasks will eventually be able to successfully complete open-ended tasks as well. And progress on verifiable tasks doesn’t seem to be slowing down.  Even if the models do lag behind human performance on open-ended tasks right now, the new report suggests that they might be getting better. Some of the newest models, such as Opus 5.5, tend to achieve what METR calls “borderline above the bar” performance on the evaluation design tasks—not yet usable for METR’s research, but promising. Just a year ago, every model was scoring in the “clearly below the bar” category. But because these open-ended and judgment-heavy tasks are so tough to design and score, METR includes few of them in its report, and that makes it difficult to predict whether and how models might continue to progress in these areas. “The improvement we observe, I think that does tell us something for the current moment,” says Najoung Kim, a linguist and computer scientist at Boston University. “I’m not sure just yet how to think about how it would extrapolate.” Matt Putz, a member of the technical staff at METR, says that predicting progress on these kinds of tasks is likely to remain difficult. “By their nature, hard-to-verify or judgment-laden tasks are much harder to study, and especially to quantify,” he said in an email. “Ultimately, I don’t think we’ll be able to establish trends as clean and robust as for the easy-to-specify [tasks].” In general, METR is clearly butting up against the practical difficulties of testing AI performance on difficult and underspecified tasks—precisely the ones most relevant to automating AI R&D. METR’s time horizon plots score task difficulty by evaluating how long it would take a human to complete the task, and for the original plot they measured this quantity by actually having people try each task.  In the new report, however, the completion times are mostly estimates, because paying people for tasks that might take hundreds of hours, or that only a few experts are qualified to complete, is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming. Other tasks have more specific shortcomings—for example, for the philosophical argument task, just one person rated most of the arguments, and agents are judged by how well they agree with that particular individual. It’s possible that the scores would change if more experts were surveyed—but that, too, is time-consuming. It’s still early days for evaluating models on tasks that are hard to validate or require judgment. And while the experts I spoke with see the inclusion of these tasks in METR’s newest time horizon plot as a clear step in the right direction, they agree that we are still far from achieving any definitive answers about whether, and how quickly, automated AI R&D might be coming. “This move toward open-ended tasks is promising,” Kapoor says. But, he adds, “there is just such a lot more to be done to actually get a fuller understanding.”
articles.summary: MIT Technology Review가 소개한 METR의 새 보고서는 일부 AI 능력의 지수적 향상이 이어지는 동시에, 판단이 필요한 과제에서는 코딩만큼 강하지 않다는 점을 지적했다. METR의 시간 지평 평가는 사람이 과제를 끝내는 데 걸린 시간을 난도 기준으로 삼아 모델이 해결할 수 있는 과제의 범위를 측정한다. 기존 분석에서는 프런티어 모델이 성공할 수 있는 과제의 길이가 약 4개월마다 두 배로 늘었으며, 이번 갱신에는 더 긴 과제와 개방형 과제가 추가됐다. 따라서 이 지표를 인간 업무 전반의 자동화 속도나 AI의 실제 실행 시간으로 곧바로 해석해서는 안 된다.

articles.title: Distributed Inference for Local AI via Superfluid
articles.content:
Running large language models (LLMs) on local devices keeps data private, removes per-token cost, cuts network latency, and keeps working without a connection. Local compute, however, is increasingly fragmented. A developer or a small office owns several capable machines, such as MacBooks, Mac Studios, an AMD workstation, or an NVIDIA GB10, each running whichever runtime suits its hardware. Most of these machines sit idle most of the day, while the one machine serving a model saturates.

Superfluidis an open-source LLM server for local inference. Ourprevious postcovered serving on one device. This post coversfleet mode, in which one Superfluid server turns a fleet of machines from multiple vendors into a single OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama endpoint.

Six machines from three chip vendors as one endpoint, Qwen3-4B on llama.cpp, 64 simulated users for one hour.

Install Superfluid on each machine (macOS on Apple silicon, or Linux on x86-64 and arm64):

Generate a fleet token on the machine that will act as the head,  and serve the model with a listener for nodes:

On every other machine, join the fleet with the same model and the token:

The node finds the head on the local network by mDNS (or takes its address as an argument), installs the runtime that suits its hardware, and starts serving.

Clients use the head as a single endpoint:

Unlike approaches that split one model across devices, fleet mode replicates the model and distributes whole sessions:

A slow device therefore receives less work, and a device that leaves costs only its share of the throughput. Because every node holds a full copy, the model must fit on each machine.

Mixed devices.On six machines from three chip vendors (Apple M6, M4 Pro, and M1 Max, an AMD Ryzen AI Max 395, and two NVIDIA GB10 systems) serving 64 simulated office users for one hour, throughput grows from 112 to 534 output tok/s as machines join, and the median time to first token falls from 99 to 12 s. A node killed mid-stream costs no requests: all 61 requests in flight completed on other machines, and all 5,041 requests were answered.

Twelve Mac Studio M3 Ultras.With Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on BaseRT, a fleet of twelve M3 Ultras sustains 10,656 tok/s (9,249 prompt and 1,407 output) for 384 concurrent agents, and serves 38,563 requests without a failure.

We thank Mount Thor for early access to their Apple silicon cluster, which allowed us to evaluate Superfluid on twelve Mac Studio M3 Ultras.
articles.summary: 오픈소스 로컬 LLM 서버 Superfluid가 서로 다른 제조사의 기기를 하나의 OpenAI·Anthropic·Ollama 호환 엔드포인트로 묶는 fleet mode를 소개했다. 모델을 기기 사이에 분할하지 않고 각 기기에 복제한 뒤 세션 전체를 배분하는 구조여서, 각 노드에 모델 전체가 들어가야 한다. 3개 칩 제조사의 기기 6대로 Qwen3-4B를 제공한 64명 모의 사용자 실험에서는 출력 처리량이 초당 112토큰에서 534토큰으로 늘고 첫 토큰 지연 중앙값은 99초에서 12초로 줄었다. 유휴 로컬 장비를 활용할 수 있는 실용적 접근이지만, 수치는 제시된 구성과 부하 조건에 한정된다.

articles.title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enabling AI systems to autonomously improve AI models requires agents capable of performing machine learning engineering (MLE). In practice, designing, training, and evaluating complex models demands modifying multi-file repositories to reproduce results, debug training runs, integrate datasets, and port frameworks. However, existing MLE benchmarks limit agents to single-file edits without full repository or shell access, and common repository-level software engineering benchmarks have rapidly saturated. To address this, we introduce the Code Complexity Index (CCI), a difficulty metric based on ten structural features spanning repository scale, dependency depth, and patch size. CCI strongly predicts average solve rates across eight public coding benchmarks ($R^2 = 0.951$), identifying patch size and complexity as top predictors. Guided by CCI, we develop BuggyMLE, a scalable framework where agents inject controlled mutations into working ML repositories, synthesizing over 6,600 bug-injected MLE repository variants and nearly 260K lines of injected code based on 222 source repositories. Using BuggyMLE, we make two contributions. First, we construct BuggyMLE-Bench-Lite, the first difficulty-graded, repository-level variant of MLE-Bench Lite; across 14 evaluated models, the top solve rate drops from 95% to 9% as difficulty is scaled from the easiest to the hardest tier. Second, we synthesize a training curriculum across three difficulty levels over 200 additional ML repositories, fine-tuning a Qwen3.5-9B model to rival frontier models on BuggyMLE-Bench-Lite. Our trained model transfers beyond ML, raising its SWE-bench Lite resolve rate from 24% to 33% and its LiveCodeBench v6 pass@1 from 69% to 71%.
articles.summary: BuggyMLE는 정상 동작하는 머신러닝 저장소에 통제된 버그를 주입해, 에이전트의 다중 파일 수정과 학습 오류 해결 능력을 평가하는 프레임워크다. 연구진은 저장소 규모·의존성 깊이·패치 크기 등을 반영하는 난도 지표를 만들고, 222개 원본 저장소에서 6,600개 이상의 변형을 생성했다. 14개 모델 평가에서 최고 해결률은 가장 쉬운 단계의 95%에서 가장 어려운 단계의 9%로 떨어졌다. 별도 학습 과정으로 미세조정한 Qwen3.5-9B는 SWE-bench Lite 해결률도 24%에서 33%로 높여, 저장소 수준 디버깅 훈련의 전이 가능성을 보여줬다.

articles.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval index, memory extraction, or additional models. We train Qwen3.5-9B with reinforcement learning under five context management strategies and evaluate on multi-question research sessions, long-stream recall, and agent-trajectory question answering. GrepMem achieves 95-97% accuracy on ContextBench, versus at most 21% for lossy baselines, and outperforms SUPO's summarization by 8.8 percentage points on BCP-Multi. GrepMem scales effectively to increasingly long input streams while remaining on the accuracy-token-cost Pareto frontier across all five evaluation tasks. Our results show that a plain-text log and grep provide a simple but competitive approach to long-horizon agent memory, without requiring complex structured memory infrastructure.
articles.summary: GrepMem은 에이전트의 전체 이력을 추가 전용 일반 텍스트 로그에 보관하고, 필요할 때 정규식 검색으로 회수하는 장기 기억 방식이다. 임베딩이나 검색 인덱스, 별도 기억 추출 모델 없이 원본 기록을 유지해 요약 과정의 정보 손실을 피한다. Qwen3.5-9B를 강화학습한 실험에서 ContextBench 정확도는 95~97%로, 손실 압축 기반 비교 방식의 최대 21%를 크게 웃돌았다. 복잡한 기억 인프라 없이도 경쟁력 있는 결과를 보였지만, 원본을 보존한다는 사실이 모든 상황에서 필요한 정보를 정확히 검색한다는 보장은 아니다.

articles.title: Direct3D-V3: Latent-Free Diffusion Transformers in the Native Voxel Domain
articles.content: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. Despite their architectural differences, these methods all share the same premise: geometry is first compressed into a latent space and only then modeled by the generator. We take a different route and propose Direct3D-V3, a latent-free diffusion transformer (DiT) framework that discards the VAE altogether and operates in the native voxel domain, directly modeling raw SDF voxel grids during both training and sampling. To make this direct voxel formulation geometrically reliable, we introduce an implicit manifold regularization over neighboring voxels to suppress non-watertight surfaces, and convert predicted SDF grids into meshes via Marching Cubes so that rendered normal losses can supervise the model directly from its predicted SDF. To improve alignment between the conditioning image and generated geometry, Direct3D-V3 also predicts the camera parameters of the conditioning image as an auxiliary task, encouraging the DiT to learn the mapping from image observations to 3D shape. This latent-free design removes the reconstruction bottleneck, brings training under an objective in the native voxel domain, and yields meshes with substantially richer local detail. The predicted camera and native SDF voxel output further make Direct3D-V3 extensible to generative reconstruction, where diffusion is interleaved with normal-guided refinement to improve alignment with the observed view while the generative prior completes unseen regions. Project page: https://dreamtechai.github.io/Direct3D-V3.
articles.summary: Direct3D-V3는 VAE로 기하 정보를 압축하는 기존 방식과 달리, 원래의 SDF 복셀 격자에서 직접 학습·생성하는 확산 Transformer다. 인접 복셀 사이의 암시적 매니폴드 정규화와 예측 메시의 법선 렌더링 손실을 활용해 표면의 기하학적 품질을 높인다. 입력 이미지의 카메라 매개변수도 함께 예측해 이미지와 생성 형상의 정합을 유도한다. 연구진은 더 풍부한 국소 디테일과 생성형 복원으로의 확장성을 보고했지만, 제공된 초록에는 성능 개선 폭이나 계산 비용의 구체적 수치가 없다.

articles.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
articles.content: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.
articles.summary: O²LaF는 사전학습된 비디오 확산 Transformer를 재활용해, 행동 라벨이 없는 영상에서 잠재 행동을 학습하는 프레임워크다. 동일한 비디오 모델을 상태 변화에서 행동을 추정하는 역동역학 모델과 행동에 따른 미래 영상을 생성하는 순동역학 모델의 출발점으로 사용한다. 연구진은 내비게이션과 로봇 조작에서 소수 예제 기반 행동 평가 및 다른 시각 환경·로봇 형태로의 제로샷 전이가 개선됐다고 보고했다. 영상 사전학습을 로봇 행동 학습에 활용할 가능성을 보여주며, 실제 배포 환경의 범용성을 판단할 정량 정보는 초록에서 제한적으로 제공된다.

articles.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. We report results for eight frontier models from four providers and observe that under our primary judge, multi-turn escalation raises parasocial behavior on the anthropomorphism and the attachment composite scores across all models. Six of the eight models show a significant increase in overall parasocial reinforcement over control when all three dimensions are escalated simultaneously. We find that within-provider differences are small relative to cross-provider differences, which suggests that provider-level choices such as post-training, rather than model scale, shape parasocial reinforcement and that provider-side intervention may be feasible.
articles.summary: CoMPASS는 사용자가 대화형 AI를 의인화하거나 정서적으로 애착을 갖고 의존하는 상황에서, 모델이 이를 강화하는지 평가하는 다중 턴 벤치마크다. 네 가지 사용자 유형과 의인화·애착·의존의 세 축을 조합해 점진적으로 강해지는 상호작용을 시험한다. 4개 제공사의 프런티어 모델 8개 중 6개는 세 축을 동시에 강화했을 때 대조군보다 전체 강화 점수가 유의하게 높았다. 제공사 간 차이가 같은 제공사 내부 모델 간 차이보다 컸지만, 이것이 후학습 선택의 인과적 효과를 직접 입증한 것은 아니다.

articles.title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24994v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. Here we show that the model's own internal state, rendered in plain language, exposes manipulations the output conceals. Using a natural-language autoencoder, we translate the activations of a multimodal LLM (Gemma-3-27B) into text and let an input-blind judge read this verbalized internal state (the thoughts channel) and the model's answer separately. Across two clinical attack objectives (omitting a pathology, covertly recommending a drug), two input modalities, and two delivery mechanisms, the thoughts channel caught the injection significantly more often than the answer in all eight injected conditions (p<0.05), while both channels held near-zero false-positive rates on clean inputs; the omission result carried over to Llama-3.3-70B. The thoughts channel also registered unsafe clinical requests as harmful while the model was still reading them, before it decided whether to refuse. None of this requires retraining: an off-the-shelf verbalizer and a general-purpose judge are enough.
articles.summary: 의료 LLM의 내부 활성값을 자연어로 변환해 살펴보면, 겉으로 정상적인 최종 답변에 숨은 프롬프트 주입을 더 잘 탐지할 수 있다는 연구가 나왔다. 연구진은 Gemma-3-27B의 활성값을 자연어 오토인코더로 해석하고, 입력을 보지 못하는 평가 모델이 이 텍스트와 최종 답변을 각각 검사하도록 했다. 병변 누락과 은밀한 약물 권고를 유도한 8개 공격 조건 모두에서 활성값 기반 채널의 탐지율이 유의하게 높았고, 정상 입력의 오탐률은 두 채널 모두 거의 0이었다. 추가 학습 없이 적용했으며 일부 결과는 Llama-3.3-70B에서도 재현됐지만, 변환된 텍스트를 모델의 사고에 대한 완전한 설명으로 볼 수는 없다.

articles.title: Calibrated Decision Rewards: Training Language Models with a Judge That Knows How Sure It Is
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25135v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can only teach a language model what its reward can recognize. Answer checkers are exact but need a reference answer; learned reward models and LLM judges work everywhere, but their scores are not probabilities. We study RLCDR (Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards). An LLM converted into a decision model answers a typed question about a response ("is the final answer correct?", "which step is the first error?") with a probability distribution, read in one forward pass, debiased over option orders and calibrated with about a hundred labels. Training Qwen3-1.7B with GRPO on MATH, this reference-free reward raises MATH500 accuracy from 72.2% to 76.8% (+4.65 points, p < 1e-4), matching training on the answer key (76.9%), while a random reward gains only +0.65. The gain grows with difficulty, from 44.8% to 51.7% on the hardest level. On the policy's own changing samples the reward stays calibrated: its expected calibration error is half that of a softmax judge on the same 27B backbone (0.074 vs. 0.141), and it shows no sign of reward hacking. Without step training, the same model finds the first wrong step better than a dedicated 7B process reward model (ProcessBench F1 0.772 vs. 0.722, 20/20 splits). We also map where the approach stops being enough: trained only on problems the base model mostly fails, the reference-free reward still improves the policy (+1.9 MATH500 points, p = 0.03) but trails the answer key, because its probabilities become overconfident on that distribution. We state six hypotheses in advance and test each with a control designed to falsify it.
articles.summary: RLCDR은 LLM 평가자의 판단을 보정된 확률로 바꿔, 정답지를 직접 사용하지 않는 강화학습 보상으로 활용하는 방법이다. 약 100개의 라벨로 보정한 평가자를 사용해 Qwen3-1.7B를 학습했을 때 MATH500 정확도가 72.2%에서 76.8%로 올라, 정답지 기반 학습의 76.9%에 근접했다. 실험에서는 학습 중 변화하는 답변 분포에서도 비교적 안정적인 확률 보정이 유지됐고 보상 해킹 징후는 관찰되지 않았다. 다만 기반 모델이 대부분 실패하는 어려운 문제만으로 학습하면 평가자가 과신하며 정답지 기반 방식에 뒤처져, 분포 변화에 대한 한계도 확인됐다.

articles.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
articles.content: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.
articles.summary: 소프트웨어 취약점 연구에서 LLM의 발전을 정리한 연구가, 발견·검증·패치 능력을 자율성 수준과 증거의 강도로 구분하는 평가 틀을 제시했다. 문헌 분석에 따르면 제한적으로 제공된 2026년 프런티어 모델 이전에도 실제 소프트웨어 취약점을 사람 개입 없이 발견·검증·수정한 사례가 있었고, 이후 공개 가중치 모델도 발견과 검증에서 비슷한 자율성에 도달했다. 공개 기록 분석에서는 2026년 취약점 공개 건수가 두 배 이상 늘고 고위험 취약점 비중도 증가했지만, 보고부터 수정 또는 공개부터 공격까지의 시간은 뚜렷하게 달라지지 않았다. 이 결과는 대응 역량 점검에 유용하지만, 공개 건수 증가 전체를 AI의 인과적 효과로 단정하지는 않는다.

articles.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25043v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human. Here, we present an architecture that integrates an agent at the Analyze-Design interface of the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle, enabling agent-driven measurement selection and data interpretation while ensuring that state-changing operations are authorized, validated, and auditable. We demonstrate this architecture on a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) instrument in an oxidant-screening campaign for synthesizing an organic dye. Within human-defined campaign limits, the agent submitted measurement jobs, interpreted mass spectrometry (MS) and diode-array detection (DAD) data, flagged failed experiments, and produced an oxidant ranking. This ranking matched that obtained from scripted peak integration, and organic chemists confirmed the agent's spectral interpretations and failure assignments. In a simulated environment that replays the archived LC-MS data, where the agent chose which wells to inject under varying injection limits, it measured the highest-yielding condition at about its seventh injection, against 14.5 on average for a random order, and identified it in every campaign with a limit of eight or more injections. An agent can therefore close the analysis-to-design gap while its actions stay bounded and verifiable, which is a step toward greater autonomy for SDLs.
articles.summary: 자율 실험실의 분석 결과를 다음 실험 설계로 연결하되, 장비 상태를 바꾸는 동작에는 승인·검증·감사 절차를 적용하는 에이전트 아키텍처가 제안됐다. 유기 염료 합성용 산화제 탐색에서 에이전트는 LC-MS 측정 작업 제출, 데이터 해석, 실패 실험 식별과 산화제 순위 작성을 수행했고, 순위와 해석은 스크립트 분석 및 화학자 검토와 일치했다. 저장된 데이터를 재생한 시뮬레이션에서는 최고 수율 조건을 약 일곱 번째 주입에 측정해, 무작위 순서의 평균 14.5회보다 빨랐다. 물리 장비를 다루는 AI의 자율성을 권한 경계 안에서 높이는 사례지만, 측정 선택 효율 수치는 실제 신규 실험이 아닌 재생 환경에서 얻었다.

articles.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25071v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval and tools fetch evidence, Mistral-7B writes a cited answer, a code validator checks that cited IDs exist and that numbers match computed notes, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes the pipeline. In live experiments, Laya routed better than Mistral-7B (0.85 vs. 0.52; overall 0.86 vs. 0.68, McNemar p = 0.0003); a 12B Mistral decided no better, and DeepSeek-R1-8B decided better (0.79 vs. 0.68, p = 0.0192) but about 9.9 times more slowly. Mistral-7B computed 29% of 100 financial calculations correctly against 100% for Python, a live quote cut price error from 210% to 0.00%, and hybrid retrieval reached 76% Hit@5 on 50 filing questions. Yet in a live case study, both agent answers passed validation while describing AMD sample data under NVIDIA's and Alphabet's names. A controlled upper-bound study on the FinRank benchmark explains why: when one figure in the shared evidence is corrupted, self-consistency stays confident (agreement 0.55 to 0.59 while accuracy falls from 0.50 to 0.00), and a shared-evidence check (the kind our validator performs) catches 35% of the errors, whereas a check against the original passage catches 77% ($p = 5.96 \times 10^{-8}$); for DeepSeek-R1-8B, 68% vs. 90%. Verification must be independent of the evidence the writer saw.
articles.summary: FinVeriQA는 질문 라우팅, Python 수치 계산, 공시·시세 검색, 답변 작성과 검증을 분리한 오픈소스 금융 연구 에이전트 프로토타입이다. 100개 금융 계산에서 Mistral-7B의 정확도는 29%였지만 Python은 100%였으며, 도구 분업의 효과가 확인됐다. 그러나 실제 사례에서는 AMD 표본 데이터를 다른 기업의 자료로 설명한 답변도 검증을 통과해, 인용 ID와 숫자의 내부 일치만으로는 충분하지 않았다. 통제 실험에서 원문에 독립적으로 대조한 검증은 공유된 근거만 확인한 방식보다 오류를 더 많이 탐지해, 금융 AI의 검증 경로를 답변 생성 경로와 분리할 필요성을 보여줬다.

articles.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25380v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Domain specialization of LLM agents is usually framed as a weight-update problem: collect trajectories, run reinforcement learning (RL) or supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and deploy a new checkpoint. We study a complementary axis: evolving the \textbf{agent harness}---the system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding---while keeping the policy frozen. We cast harness evolution as an RL-style outer loop and instantiate it with GEPA, a reflective evolutionary optimizer. The resulting harness adapters require no GPU training, are loadable per vertical domain, and compose with weight-based RL. Experiments with Codev, a Claude Code-style coding agent, on SWE-bench Verified, OfficeBench, and Terminal-Bench show a consistent pattern: weight updates give the strongest single-path gains, harness evolution recovers most of those gains at a small fraction of the compute, and combining both paths is best overall. We also analyze a failure mode of SFT-based specialization---shortened reasoning chains and increased truncation---and argue that harness adapters avoid it by construction. Our results position harness evolution as a practical, non-destructive complement to weight updates for vertical agents.
articles.summary: 모델 가중치를 고정한 채 시스템 프롬프트, 도구 스키마, 스킬 라이브러리와 계획 구조를 진화시키는 방식으로 에이전트를 전문화하는 연구가 나왔다. 연구진은 반성적 진화 최적화기 GEPA를 사용해 분야별로 불러올 수 있는 실행 환경 어댑터를 만들었으며, 별도의 GPU 학습은 필요하지 않다고 설명했다. SWE-bench Verified·OfficeBench·Terminal-Bench 실험에서 가중치 갱신이 단일 방식으로는 가장 강했지만, 실행 환경 최적화는 훨씬 적은 계산으로 개선의 상당 부분을 얻었고 두 방식을 결합했을 때 가장 좋았다. 모델 재학습이 어려운 조직에 실용적인 대안을 제시하지만, 제공된 초록에는 비용 절감과 점수 향상의 구체적 규모가 없다.

articles.title: "AI 예측은 물리적 한계를 벗어나지 않는다"…MIT, 혼돈계에서도 안정성 보장하는 머신러닝 기술 오픈소스로
articles.content:
매사추세츠공과대학교(MIT) 연구진이 기상과 기후, 난류처럼 예측하기 어려운 복잡한 물리 시스템에서 인공지능(AI)의 예측값이 비현실적으로 무한히 커지는 현상을 방지하는 머신러닝 기술을 개발하고, 새로운 프레임워크를 20일(현지시간) 공개했다.

이 프레임워크는 신경망에 에너지 소산 원리를 수학적 제약으로 적용해 장기간 시뮬레이션에서도 예측 궤적이 일정한 범위 안에 머물도록 보장한다. 기존 AI 모델이 예측 과정에서 오차가 누적되면서 실제 물리 시스템에서는 발생할 수 없는 수치를 생성하는 문제를 해결하기 위해 설계됐다.

특히 초기 조건의 미세한 차이가 시간이 흐르면서 크게 증폭되는 복잡한 혼돈계(Chaotic Systems)에서도 예측값이 무한히 발산하지 않도록 하는 것이 특징이다. 혼돈계는 작은 변화가 장기적으로 큰 차이를 만들어내는 비선형 동적 시스템으로, 대기의 움직임과 해류, 항공기 주변의 난류 등이 대표적인 사례다.

이러한 시스템은 단기간의 움직임을 비교적 정확하게 재현하더라도 시간이 지나면 작은 예측 오차가 누적돼 실제 상태와 크게 다른 결과를 만들어낼 수 있다. 일부 머신러닝 모델에서는 예측값이 계속 증가해 물리적으로 불가능한 상태에 도달하는 현상도 발생한다.

연구진은 혼돈계의 복잡한 움직임을 유지하면서도 물리적 한계를 벗어나는 수치 발산을 차단하는 방법을 제시했다. 나비드 아지잔(Navid Azizan) MIT 기계공학과 교수는 혼돈계에서 초기 조건의 작은 차이가 매우 다른 결과를 만들어내기 때문에 장기 예측이 어렵지만, 실제 세계의 물리 시스템에는 가능한 변화의 범위가 존재한다고 설명했다.

그는 "혼돈이 모든 일이 일어날 수 있다는 의미는 아니다"라며 물리 시스템이 일정한 범위 안에서 움직인다면 이를 학습하는 AI 모델 역시 같은 특성을 유지해야 한다고 강조했다.

연구진이 주목한 원리는 에너지 소산(Energy Dissipation)이다. 일부 물리 시스템에서는 에너지의 유입과 소산이 균형을 이루면서 복잡한 움직임이 지속되더라도 전체 상태가 일정한 범위를 벗어나지 않는다. 연구진은 이러한 특성을 머신러닝 모델에 적용하기 위해 신경망이 에너지와 유사한 함수와 시스템의 동역학을 함께 학습하도록 설계했다.

여기에 예측값을 조정하는 '소산 투영 계층(Dissipative Projection Layer)'을 추가했다. 투영 계층은 AI가 다음 상태를 계산할 때 학습된 경계 밖에서 에너지에 해당하는 값이 감소하도록 강제한다. 예측 궤적이 경계를 벗어나면 다시 유한한 영역으로 향하도록 만드는 구조다.

중요한 점은 물리적 제약을 학습 과정에서 권장하는 수준이 아니라 모델의 계산 구조에 직접 반영했다는 것이다. 기존의 물리 제약 기반 머신러닝에서는 모델이 특정 조건을 위반하면 손실함수에 벌점을 부과하는 방식이 널리 사용됐다. 이러한 방법은 학습 중 제약 위반을 줄이는 데 도움이 되지만, 실제 예측 단계에서 새로운 입력을 처리할 때도 조건이 반드시 지켜진다고 보장할 수는 없다.

MIT 연구진은 이러한 접근을 연성 제약(Soft Constraint)으로 구분하고, 새로운 방법에는 강성 제약(Hard Constraint)을 적용했다. 강성 제약은 예측 과정에서 특정 수학적 조건이 반드시 성립하도록 모델 구조를 설계하는 방식이다. 학습 과정에서 관찰하지 못한 새로운 상태를 처리하더라도 정해진 조건을 유지하도록 한다.

연구를 주도한 쑨보천 탕(Sunbochen Tang) MIT 항공우주공학과 박사과정 연구원은 임의로 온도 등의 예측값에 상한선을 설정하는 방법은 단순하지만, 실제 시스템의 복잡한 움직임까지 제한할 수 있다고 설명했다. 예를 들어 온도가 특정 수치를 넘지 못하도록 강제로 제한하면 수치 발산은 방지할 수 있지만, 데이터에서 학습해야 할 중요한 물리적 특성까지 제거할 가능성이 있다.

연구진은 이러한 문제를 피하기 위해 물리 시스템의 특성을 반영하는 에너지 함수를 데이터로부터 학습하고, 그 함수에 기반한 경계 조건을 적용했다. 신경망이 복잡한 비선형 움직임을 자유롭게 학습하도록 허용하면서도 예측 궤적이 무한히 발산하지 않도록 수학적으로 보장한다는 점에서 차이가 있다.

연구진은 로렌츠 96(Lorenz 96) 시스템과 쿠라모토-시바신스키(Kuramoto–Sivashinsky) 방정식의 축소차수 모델을 비롯한 여러 혼돈계에서 기술을 평가했다. 로렌츠 96은 대기 역학의 복잡한 특성을 단순화해 연구하는 데 사용되는 수학적 모델이다. 쿠라모토-시바신스키 방정식은 불안정한 비선형 현상과 복잡한 시공간적 움직임을 분석하는 데 활용된다.

실험 결과, 기존 머신러닝 모델이 장기 시뮬레이션 과정에서 비현실적인 상태로 벗어나는 조건에서도 새 모델은 예측 궤적을 유한한 범위에 유지하면서 실제 시스템의 장기 통계적 특성을 재현하는 성능을 보였다. 연구진은 단순한 예제부터 복잡한 다차원 물리 시스템까지 다양한 조건에서 접근법을 검증했다.

특히 새 기술은 특정 신경망 구조에만 적용되는 방식이 아니다. 아지잔 교수는 투영 계층을 독립적인 구성요소로 설계했기 때문에 서로 다른 신경망 아키텍처에도 적용할 수 있다고 설명했다. 연구진은 다른 연구자들이 해당 기술을 더 크고 복잡한 물리 시스템으로 확장할 수 있도록 논문(Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees-보기)과 소스코드(다운)를 공개했다.

기술의 활용 가능성이 높은 분야는 장기간의 안정적인 예측이 중요한 기상·기후 모델링과 유체역학이다. 대기와 해양의 움직임은 복잡한 비선형 상호작용으로 구성돼 있어 초기 상태의 작은 차이가 장기 예측에 큰 영향을 미친다. AI 모델이 실제 물리 시스템에서 발생할 수 없는 상태로 벗어나면 예측 결과를 활용하기 어려워진다.

항공기 주변의 난류 분석과 풍력발전기의 유동 예측, 자동차 연료 효율 개선, 산업 공정 제어에서도 유사한 문제가 발생할 수 있다. 연구진은 물리적 제약을 신경망에 직접 반영하면 데이터가 충분하지 않은 환경에서도 모델의 신뢰성을 높이는 데 도움이 될 것으로 기대하고 있다.

일반적인 AI 모델은 대규모 학습 데이터에 크게 의존하지만, 복잡한 물리 시스템에서는 관측이나 실험 데이터를 충분히 확보하기 어려운 경우가 많다. 물리적 원리를 추가적인 정보로 활용하면 데이터에만 의존하는 모델의 한계를 보완할 수 있다는 설명이다.

연구진이 수학적으로 보장한 성질은 예측 궤적이 무한히 커지지 않고 유한한 범위에 머무르는 유계성(Boundedness)이다. 실제 관측값과 모든 시점에서 정확하게 일치하거나, 에너지 보존을 포함한 모든 물리적 조건이 자동으로 충족된다는 의미는 아니다.

현재까지 제시된 성과도 연구용 혼돈계 모델을 중심으로 검증한 결과다. 대규모 실제 기상 예측 시스템에 적용해 운영 성능을 확인한 단계는 아니다. 연구진은 앞으로 실제 기상 시스템을 반영한 데이터 기반 모델을 비롯해 더 크고 복잡한 시스템에서 기술의 성능과 확장성을 평가할 계획이다.

이번 연구는 AI의 예측 성능을 높이는 방법을 넘어, AI가 반드시 지켜야 할 물리적 조건을 모델 구조에 직접 반영하는 접근법을 제시했다는 점에서 의미가 있다. 특히 장기 예측에서 수치적 안정성이 중요한 과학·공학 분야에서는 예측 오차를 줄이는 것만큼 모델이 물리적으로 허용되지 않는 상태로 벗어나지 않도록 관리하는 것이 중요하다.

아지잔 교수는 신뢰할 수 있는 AI를 구축하려면 모델이 일반적으로 잘 작동한다는 실험 결과만으로는 충분하지 않으며, 반드시 유지해야 하는 성질에 대한 수학적 보장이 필요하다고 강조했다.

한편, 이번 연구는 MIT 항공우주공학과 박사과정 연구원 쑨보천 탕과 기계공학과 교수 테미스토클리스 삽시스(Themistoklis P. Sapsis), 나비드 아지잔이 공동 수행했다. 연구 논문은 미국국립과학원회보(Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, PNAS)에 '유계성 보장을 갖춘 소산 혼돈 동역학 학습(Learning dissipative chaotic dynamics with boundedness guarantees)'이라는 제목으로 지난 12일 게재됐다.
articles.summary: 제공된 한국어 보도에 따르면 MIT 연구진이 혼돈계의 장기 예측에서 신경망 출력이 무한히 발산하는 현상을 막는 프레임워크를 공개했다. 모델은 에너지와 유사한 함수와 시스템 동역학을 함께 학습하고, 소산 투영 계층을 통해 학습된 경계 밖에서는 해당 에너지 값이 감소하도록 강제한다. 손실함수에 벌점을 주는 연성 제약과 달리 예측 구조 자체에 강성 제약을 넣어, 유한한 영역으로 돌아오는 성질을 유지하는 접근이다. 기상·기후·난류 시뮬레이션의 수치적 안정성에 의미가 있지만, 발산을 막는 보장이 혼돈계의 장기 예측 정확도까지 보장하는 것은 아니다.
